passages.text: Then Job answered: “I have heard many things like these; miserable comforters are you all.
passages.sermon:
Job was a righteous man who suffered greatly.
His friends tried to comfort him.
Job answered them.
He said, “I have heard many things like these before.
All of you are miserable comforters.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ שָׁמַ֣עְתִּי כְאֵ֣לֶּה רַבּ֑וֹת מְנַחֲמֵ֖י עָמָ֣ל כֻּלְּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Is there no end to your long-winded speeches? What provokes you to continue testifying?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
Job hears their many words.
Job asks if their speeches will ever end.
Job calls their words long-winded.
Job asks what drives them to keep answering him.
Job wants to know why they continue to speak.
passages.original: הֲקֵ֥ץ לְדִבְרֵי־ ר֑וּחַ א֥וֹ מַה־ יַּ֝מְרִֽיצְךָ֗ כִּ֣י תַעֲנֶֽה׃

passages.text: I could also speak like you if you were in my place; I could heap up words against you and shake my head at you.
passages.sermon:
Job is the speaker.
Job is suffering greatly.
Job’s friends have tried to comfort him, but their words have failed.
Job addresses his friends.

I could speak just like you.
If you were suffering as I am now, I could do what you do.
I could pile up words against you.
I could shake my head at you.
passages.original: גַּ֤ם׀ אָנֹכִי֮ כָּכֶ֪ם אֲדַ֫בֵּ֥רָה ל֤וּ־ יֵ֪שׁ נַפְשְׁכֶ֡ם תַּ֤חַת נַפְשִׁ֗י אַחְבִּ֣ירָה עֲלֵיכֶ֣ם בְּמִלִּ֑ים וְאָנִ֥יעָה עֲ֝לֵיכֶ֗ם בְּמ֣וֹ רֹאשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: But I would encourage you with my mouth, and the consolation of my lips would bring relief.
passages.sermon:
I would speak to you with my mouth.
I would give you encouragement.
My lips would offer you comfort.
My words would bring you relief.
passages.original: אֲאַמִּצְכֶ֥ם בְּמוֹ־ פִ֑י וְנִ֖יד שְׂפָתַ֣י יַחְשֹֽׂךְ׃

passages.text: Even if I speak, my pain is not relieved, and if I hold back, how will it go away?
passages.sermon: Job is suffering deeply.\r\nHe says, “If I speak, my pain does not stop.”\r\nHe also says, “If I stay silent, my pain does not leave me.”
passages.original: אִֽם־ אֲ֭דַבְּרָה לֹא־ יֵחָשֵׂ֣ךְ כְּאֵבִ֑י וְ֝אַחְדְּלָ֗ה מַה־ מִנִּ֥י יַהֲלֹֽךְ׃

passages.text: Surely He has now exhausted me; You have devastated all my family.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a righteous man who suffers greatly.
God has allowed Job to experience deep suffering.
Now, God has made me tired and weak.
God has destroyed all my family.
passages.original: אַךְ־ עַתָּ֥ה הֶלְאָ֑נִי הֲ֝שִׁמּ֗וֹתָ כָּל־ עֲדָתִֽי׃

passages.text: You have bound me, and it has become a witness; my frailty rises up and testifies against me.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in deep suffering.
God has bound Job.
This binding stands as a witness.
Job’s weakness rises up.
His frailty testifies against him.
His suffering is clear before everyone.
passages.original: וַֽ֭תִּקְמְטֵנִי לְעֵ֣ד הָיָ֑ה וַיָּ֥קָם בִּ֥י כַ֝חֲשִׁ֗י בְּפָנַ֥י יַעֲנֶֽה׃

passages.text: His anger has torn me and opposed me; He gnashes His teeth at me. My adversary pierces me with His eyes.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks about his suffering.
God is angry with Job.
God’s anger tears Job apart.
God stands against Job.
God grinds His teeth at Job.
Job’s enemy looks at him with sharp, piercing eyes.
passages.original: אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף׀ וַֽיִּשְׂטְמֵ֗נִי חָרַ֣ק עָלַ֣י בְּשִׁנָּ֑יו צָרִ֓י׀ יִלְט֖וֹשׁ עֵינָ֣יו לִֽי׃

passages.text: They open their mouths against me and strike my cheeks with contempt; they join together against me.
passages.sermon: My enemies open their mouths against me.\r\nThey strike my cheeks with contempt.\r\nThey join together against me.
passages.original: פָּעֲר֬וּ עָלַ֨י׀ בְּפִיהֶ֗ם בְּ֭חֶרְפָּה הִכּ֣וּ לְחָיָ֑י יַ֝֗חַד עָלַ֥י יִתְמַלָּאֽוּן׃

passages.text: God has delivered me to unjust men; He has thrown me to the clutches of the wicked.
passages.sermon:
God is the subject.
God has power over my life.
God has delivered me to unjust men.
God has thrown me into the hands of wicked people.
passages.original: יַסְגִּירֵ֣נִי אֵ֭ל אֶ֣ל עֲוִ֑יל וְעַל־ יְדֵ֖י רְשָׁעִ֣ים יִרְטֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: I was at ease, but He shattered me; He seized me by the neck and crushed me. He has set me up as His target; His archers surround me. He pierces my kidneys without mercy and spills my gall on the ground.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job was once at ease.
God shattered Job.
God seized Job by the neck.
God crushed Job.
God set Job up as His target.
God’s archers surround Job.
God pierces Job’s kidneys.
God shows no mercy to Job.
God spills Job’s gall on the ground.
passages.original: שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי׀ וַֽיְפַרְפְּרֵ֗נִי וְאָחַ֣ז בְּ֭עָרְפִּי וַֽיְפַצְפְּצֵ֑נִי וַיְקִימֵ֥נִי ל֝֗וֹ לְמַטָּרָֽה׃ יָ֘סֹ֤בּוּ עָלַ֨י׀ רַבָּ֗יו יְפַלַּ֣ח כִּ֭לְיוֹתַי וְלֹ֣א יַחְמ֑וֹל יִשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ לָ֝אָ֗רֶץ מְרֵרָֽתִי׃

passages.text: He breaks me with wound upon wound; He rushes me like a mighty warrior.
passages.sermon:
God attacks me again and again.
He breaks me with many wounds.
He comes at me with great force.
He rushes at me like a strong warrior.
passages.original: יִפְרְצֵ֣נִי פֶ֭רֶץ עַל־ פְּנֵי־ פָ֑רֶץ יָרֻ֖ץ עָלַ֣י כְּגִבּֽוֹר׃

passages.text: I have sewn sackcloth over my skin; I have buried my horn in the dust.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
Job says, "I have sewn sackcloth over my skin."
Sackcloth is a rough, uncomfortable cloth.
People wear sackcloth to show grief or sorrow.
Job says, "I have buried my horn in the dust."
A horn is a symbol of strength and honor.
Job means he has lost his strength and honor.
He feels humbled and brought low.
passages.original: שַׂ֣ק תָּ֭פַרְתִּי עֲלֵ֣י גִלְדִּ֑י וְעֹלַ֖לְתִּי בֶעָפָ֣ר קַרְנִֽי׃

passages.text: My face is red with weeping, and deep shadows ring my eyes; yet my hands are free of violence and my prayer is pure.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a righteous man.
Job suffers greatly.
Job says, "My face is red because I have wept."
Job says, "Dark shadows surround my eyes."
Job says, "I have not done violence with my hands."
Job says, "My prayer is pure."
passages.original: פָּנַ֣י חֳמַרְמְרָה מִנִּי־ בֶ֑כִי וְעַ֖ל עַפְעַפַּ֣י צַלְמָֽוֶת׃ עַ֭ל לֹא־ חָמָ֣ס בְּכַפָּ֑י וּֽתְפִלָּתִ֥י זַכָּֽה׃

passages.text: O earth, do not cover my blood; may my cry for help never be laid to rest.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in deep suffering.
He feels wronged and innocent.
He calls out to the earth.
He says, “Earth, do not cover my blood.”
He wants his suffering to be seen.
He says, “Do not let my cry for help be silenced.”
He wants his plea to remain heard.
passages.original: אֶ֭רֶץ אַל־ תְּכַסִּ֣י דָמִ֑י וְֽאַל־ יְהִ֥י מָ֝ק֗וֹם לְזַעֲקָתִֽי׃

passages.text: Even now my witness is in heaven, and my advocate is on high.
passages.sermon:
Job is the speaker.
Job suffers greatly.
Job feels innocent.
Job says, "Even now, my witness is in heaven."
Job says, "My advocate is on high."
Job believes someone in heaven sees his situation.
Job believes someone above will speak for him.
passages.original: גַּם־ עַ֭תָּה הִנֵּה־ בַשָּׁמַ֣יִם עֵדִ֑י וְ֝שָׂהֲדִ֗י בַּמְּרוֹמִֽים׃

passages.text: My friends are my scoffers as my eyes pour out tears to God.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is suffering.
Job’s friends mock him.
Job’s friends do not comfort him.
Job cries to God.
Job’s eyes pour out tears to God.
passages.original: מְלִיצַ֥י רֵעָ֑י אֶל־ אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַ דָּלְפָ֥ה עֵינִֽי׃

passages.text: Oh, that a man might plead with God as he pleads with his neighbor!
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in his suffering.
He wishes for something.
He wishes a man could plead with God.
He wants a man to speak to God as he speaks to his neighbor.
He desires a man to present his case to God directly.
He wants the same freedom to speak with God that he has with another person.
passages.original: וְיוֹכַ֣ח לְגֶ֣בֶר עִם־ אֱל֑וֹהַּ וּֽבֶן־ אָדָ֥ם לְרֵעֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: For when only a few years are past I will go the way of no return.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks these words.
Job is suffering.
Job knows his life is short.
He says only a few years remain for him.
He will soon die.
He will go to the grave.
He will not return from death.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ שְׁנ֣וֹת מִסְפָּ֣ר יֶאֱתָ֑יוּ וְאֹ֖רַח לֹא־ אָשׁ֣וּב אֶהֱלֹֽךְ׃
